title: Merge Sorted Lists
statement:
Merge two sorted linked lists into one sorted list.

Contract
- `first` and `second` may each be null or point to the head of an acyclic list
  whose values are already in nondecreasing order. Each node has an integer
  `value` and a mutable `next` reference.
- Return the head of a single list holding every node from both inputs, in
  nondecreasing order.
- Splice the given nodes together: do not allocate replacement nodes and do not
  change any node value. The result must contain exactly the nodes supplied.
- Merging two empty lists returns null.

Examples
- Merging `1 -> 2 -> 4` with `1 -> 3 -> 4` gives `1 -> 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 4`.
- Merging an empty list with `0` returns that same node.
- Merging two empty lists returns `null`.
hints: Both lists are already sorted, so the next node of the answer is always the smaller of the two current heads.
A throwaway head node you never return spares you from special-casing the very first link.

Advance only the list you took a node from, then attach whichever list still has nodes left and return the node after the throwaway head. Intended complexity: O(n) time in the combined length and O(1) extra space.
inputSyntax: Input: the two sorted lists separated by a semicolon, for example: [1, 2, 4]; [1, 3, 4]
